title: Strong minimality and algebraic closure

based_on.title: Pregeometries and minimal types
based_on.pages: 1–3 (§1, closure and finite bases); 8–9 (§3, terminology only; revision 2008-11-11)

based_on.title: Lecture notes on strongly minimal sets (and fields) with a generic automorphism

summary: Derive algebraic-closure exchange from finite/cofinite unary definability, then construct finite bases and prove that their size is well defined.
abstract: In an infinite set with only equality, a formula with finitely many parameters selects finitely many points or excludes finitely many points. Strong minimality requires this finite-or-cofinite behavior throughout a theory's models. It imposes a uniform bound on the finite side of each fixed formula and makes algebraic dependence reversible: if adding one parameter gives a new finite choice containing a point, that point can in turn make the added parameter algebraic. Algebraic closure consequently becomes a pregeometry, a closure operation with exchange. Finite generating sets then contain independent bases, and all finite bases of the same closed set have the same size. Equality structures and dense orders show both the strength of strong minimality and why exchange alone does not characterize it.
